title: engine:F7 — Source-defined planar-return and deadline clock procedures
description:
Persist elapsed-time clocks for planar return, declared draws, timed curses, and
other source-defined deadlines.

ROOT CAUSE: generic elapsed world timers and expiry sweeps exist, but the
source-specific procedures do not. A planar-return clock is not a duration on an
effect: it is a deadline attached to an entity that must fire correctly across
rest, travel, and session boundaries, and whose expiry has a defined narrative
and mechanical consequence. The existing engine:F7 family owns generic rest and
time orchestration, not this cross-record source-clock contract.

LEDGER ROW: capabilityId engine:F7, primitive
"planar-return-and-declared-window-clocks".
Pack membership: records whose data.executionReadiness hooks qualify as
engine:F7 with planar-return, declared-window, duration, or deadline semantics,
compared against the source clauses named by the audit.

CROSSES: engine:F3 (active-effect and owned-entity lifecycle) and engine:F6
(curse lifecycle). engine:F7 owns it.

REQUIRED INVARIANT: every source-defined deadline is a first-class persistent
clock with a defined firing consequence. A clock that silently fails to fire, or
that fires without applying its consequence, is the defect. Clocks must survive
rest, travel, and save/restore.

PROVENANCE: this bead exists because the bootstrap capability ledger
(eshyra-o9bd.19.5.1, PR #477) found this primitive had NO owner in the current
family decomposition. It was recorded there as ownershipStatus=proposed-new-bead;
this bead is that proposal made real, and the ledger row now points here.

CROSS-FAMILY PRIMITIVE. The owning family is named in the title, but the
requirement crosses family boundaries. Per the authorization criteria on
eshyra-olc5.1, a cross-family primitive is named ONCE and assigned ONE owning
family — do not re-implement it under the families it touches. Coordinate
instead.

SEQUENCING: this bead is blocked by its family's decomposition task and must not
be started before it. Decomposition does not RE-CREATE this bead; it reconciles
against it, decides whether the primitive splits further, and names the
conformance scenarios. Duplicating it under a sibling family is the failure mode
to avoid.

GREEN BAR: the nine-point definition on eshyra-o9bd.19 applies — this primitive
is not done until a provider-neutral implementation exists, reference-engine
conformance tests exercise the committed PACK representation (not a fixture),
tool exposure and state mutation are correct, unsupported input fails CLOSED,
and replay / deterministic equivalence holds where applicable.

COUNT HYGIENE: membership comes from the ledger's generated query for this
primitive. Never hand-copy a hook count into an acceptance test.

*** engine:F* IS A QUALIFIED PREFIX. engine:F1..F10 are the pack's
executionReadiness engineHooks families — NOT the CLOSED epic eshyra-2n1t's
different F1-F10, and NOT the fable:F1..F8 audit findings.
acceptance_criteria:
• Source-defined deadlines are persistent, first-class clocks, not effect durations.
• Every clock has a defined firing consequence that is applied atomically on expiry.
• Clocks survive rest, travel, and save/restore, and are correct under replay.
• Conformance tests drive the clocks from the committed pack representation.
• Unsupported or ambiguous deadline semantics fail CLOSED rather than silently not firing.
• The engine:F7 ledger membership query returns zero unowned clauses for this primitive.
